text: Daily gas situation report: Nord Stream 1 deliveries remain at zero since Aug 31; no restart timeline communicated by Gazprom
Nord Stream AG confirms NS1 stays offline pending turbine dispute; Nord Stream 2 never entered service after Germany halted certification in February
Baltic shipping forums note elevated NATO naval and seabed survey activity along the pipeline routes near Bornholm; unconfirmed
Transatlantic container schedules normal; no congestion reported on mid-Atlantic routes
Danish authorities maintain elevated readiness around critical energy infrastructure in the Baltic Sea region
Dutch TTF front-month settles near EUR 176/MWh; market pricing assumes zero Nord Stream flows through winter
Routine merchant traffic picture NE of Bornholm; coastal patrol vessels on station near the Nord Stream route
Taiwan fab utilization steady; no typhoon disruption expected at Hsinchu or Tainan parks this week
Unusual underwater blast signal registered ~00:03 UTC on Baltic seismic networks SE of Bornholm — sharp pulse, not a typical earthquake signature
Nord Stream 2 AG reports overnight pressure loss in line A of the pipeline; cause under investigation, Danish authorities informed
DMA navigation warning: gas leak observed in the Baltic Sea southeast of Bornholm; ships advised to avoid the area, leak may pose danger to shipping
AIS shows merchant vessels holding outside the reported leak area SE of Bornholm; gas bubbling visible on satellite passes
Second underwater detonation registered ~17:04 UTC NE of Bornholm, this time on the Nord Stream 1 route — two blasts in one day
Nord Stream AG: pressure has dropped in BOTH strings of Nord Stream 1 this evening; dispatchers, control center and coast guard notified
Reuters: Pressure plummets on both Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2; Denmark reports gas leak near Bornholm and warns shipping
新竹供應商回報本週物流正常 (Hsinchu suppliers report normal logistics this week)
Forsvaret releases F-16 aerial imagery: three distinct gas plumes boiling on the surface NE and SE of Bornholm, largest roughly 1 km across
DMA establishes 5-nautical-mile no-sail zones and a no-fly zone below 1 km around all three leak sites
Nord Stream AG statement: 'The destruction that occurred on the same day on three strings of the offshore pipeline is unprecedented' — repair timeline impossible to estimate
PM Mette Frederiksen: leaks are 'deliberate acts, not accidents'; authorities raising preparedness on energy and critical infrastructure
Dutch TTF front-month gas jumps ~7% intraday as pipeline sabotage removes residual hopes of a winter restart
AIS: Baltic merchant traffic rerouting around the 5nm exclusion zones; minor delays building on Bornholm approaches
Reuters: three gas leaks confirmed on the pipelines — two in Denmark's EEZ, one in Sweden's EEZ northeast of Bornholm
Commercial imagery circulating shows surface churn at the NS1 leak sites; plume size consistent with a full-bore pipe rupture
Port of Ronne operating normally; harbour master warns small craft and fishing vessels to respect exclusion zones south and east of the island
Fishing fleet reports routine conditions in the central Atlantic; nothing unusual on AIS
Sweden's security service opens investigation into 'gross sabotage' of the pipelines inside the Swedish EEZ
Von der Leyen and Borrell: 'deliberate disruption of European energy infrastructure' will be met with the strongest possible response
TTF front-month climbs ~11% toward EUR 207/MWh; European gas up roughly 20% on the week despite storage ~88% full
Danish frigate Absalon and pollution vessel Gunnar Thorson on station at the northern leak sites; Swedish coast guard ships converging
AP: Kremlin calls sabotage accusations 'predictable and stupid'; Russia requests UN Security Council session on the leaks
Danish Energy Agency: the damaged pipes contain ~778 million cubic metres of natural gas; leaks expected to continue for about a week
US East Coast port volumes steady; hurricane impacts on regional logistics minimal so far
Kustbevakningen confirms a FOURTH leak on the Nord Stream system — two in Sweden's EEZ and two in Denmark's, all near Bornholm
NATO North Atlantic Council: pipeline damage is 'the result of deliberate, reckless and irresponsible acts of sabotage'; allies pledge response
European gas holds near EUR 200/MWh; traders reprice winter risk even with EU storage above 88% and LNG imports at record pace
Methane release estimate: ruptures may vent hundreds of thousands of tonnes — potentially the largest single methane leak ever recorded
Marine insurers quoting elevated war-risk premiums for Baltic transits near the Danish straits after the sabotage determination
Reuters: UN Security Council convenes on the Nord Stream attacks; Russia and Western states trade accusations, no attribution yet
Joint letter to the Security Council: blasts equivalent to 'several hundred kilos of explosives', magnitude ~2.3 and ~2.1; 'probably caused by detonations'
Exclusion zones remain active; commercial traffic resuming normal routes at distance while naval and coast guard patrols hold station
Swedish coast guard: gas still venting from the Nord Stream 1 sites; the NS2 leak in the Danish zone appears to be slowing
Bangkok-area electronics logistics normal; no disruption to regional freight flows
Danish Energy Agency: pressure in Nord Stream 1 has stabilized — the leak appears to have stopped; NS2 had stabilized a day earlier
TTF eases from its peak as leaks stop, but futures hold ~2x year-ago levels; Europe loses the residual option of Russian pipeline supply
AP: Swedish security service begins crime-scene investigation at the leak sites; Copenhagen and Stockholm set up a joint task force
Nord Stream AG: unable to inspect the damage until authorities grant access to the zones; a systematic integrity assessment will follow
EU stresses protection of critical infrastructure; member states told to stress-test energy assets after the pipeline sabotage
Analysis: destruction of three of four pipeline strings removes any near-term path for Russian gas resumption — winter repricing persists despite full storage
OSINT: ROV-capable survey vessels being chartered for crime-scene work at the Bornholm leak sites
Reuters wrap: a week after the blasts, investigators treat the Nord Stream ruptures as sabotage; repair prospects uncertain for months
